text: The lateral ventricles are paired cavities located within the cerebral hemispheres of the brain. They contain cerebrospinal fluid.

text: The kidneys are paired organs located in the posterior abdomen, one on each side of the spine. Their visibility depends on the imaging modality and field of view.

text: A chest radiograph is an X-ray examination used to visualize structures including the lungs, heart, mediastinum, diaphragm, and portions of the bony thorax.

text: Computed tomography, or CT, uses X-rays and computer processing to produce cross-sectional images of the body.

text: An anteroposterior, or AP, radiograph is obtained when the X-ray beam travels from the anterior side of the patient toward the posterior side.

text: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscle separating the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity. It appears as curved soft-tissue structures beneath the lungs on chest radiographs.
license: Unverified provenance. Do not treat this as an authoritative citation.

text: The lung parenchyma refers to the functional tissue of the lungs. Abnormalities of the lung parenchyma may appear as changes in opacity or other radiographic findings.
license: Unverified provenance. Do not treat this as an authoritative citation.

text: An aortic aneurysm is an abnormal enlargement or dilation of a portion of the aorta. Imaging can be used to identify and characterize an aortic aneurysm.
license: Unverified provenance. Do not treat this as an authoritative citation.

text: The temporal bones are paired bones located on the sides and base of the skull. Imaging can be used to evaluate them for fractures or other abnormalities.

text: A chest x-ray is an x-ray of the chest, lungs, heart, large arteries, ribs, and diaphragm. It is a common imaging test and uses a small amount of radiation.

text: A computed tomography (CT) scan is an imaging method that uses x-rays to create pictures of cross-sections of the body. Computers combine the images into detailed slices.

text: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) uses a large magnet, radio waves, and a computer to make detailed pictures of organs and structures inside the body. MRI does not use ionizing x-ray radiation.

text: The kidneys are a pair of bean-shaped organs on either side of the spine in the back of the abdomen. They filter blood, remove waste, and help control fluid balance.
license: U.S. government MedlinePlus encyclopedia page. Short educational paraphrase for research use; verify the live page before publication.

text: An aneurysm is an abnormal widening or ballooning of a portion of an artery caused by weakness in the vessel wall. An aortic aneurysm involves the aorta, the major artery that carries blood from the heart.

text: Pneumonia is a lung infection that can cause the air sacs of the lungs to fill with fluid or pus. Chest imaging may be used as part of evaluation, but a text description cannot determine whether pneumonia is present in a particular image.

text: The brain has fluid-filled spaces called ventricles. Cerebrospinal fluid is produced in the ventricles and cushions the brain and spinal cord.

text: The diaphragm is a muscle that separates the chest cavity from the abdomen. It is the main muscle used in breathing.

text: The lateral ventricles are paired, one deep within each cerebral hemisphere. They communicate with the third ventricle and contain cerebrospinal fluid.
